claim: BASS-II investigates ignition, flame growth, flame spread and extinction limits for solid fuels burning in low-velocity forced flows under microgravity.
limitations: This record describes investigation objectives, not a specific measured result. The quantitative NASA dataset has not yet been processed in EmberScope.

claim: The BASS investigation studied the behavior of burning fuels in microgravity, including approaches to extinguishing flames and the effectiveness of nitrogen for fire suppression.
source_title: NASA - Studying Combustion and Fire Safety
limitations: This is a high-level description of the investigation. It does not establish a universal suppression effectiveness or a measured nitrogen performance value.

claim: SAFFIRE-I investigated large-scale fire growth in low gravity and low-gravity flammability limits compared with normal-gravity material flammability screening.
limitations: This record summarizes investigation objectives. It does not provide a measured flame spread rate or a quantitative fire risk score.

claim: SAME-R was designed to quantify liquid smoke particle sizes in low gravity and relate droplet size distribution to smoke generation and transport conditions.
limitations: This objective is not itself an experimental result. The quantitative measurement data has not yet been processed in EmberScope.

claim: SAME investigated smoke particle size distributions from typical spacecraft materials to support smoke detection requirements for future spacecraft.
source_title: NASA - Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
limitations: This record summarizes the investigation objective. Quantitative findings from the NASA report have not yet been extracted into the EmberScope evidence database.
